program_name: MS in Food, Nutrition, and Culinary Sciences
department_or_school: Department of Food, Nutrition, and Packaging Sciences (FNPS), College of Agriculture, Forestry and Life Sciences
spring_2027_admission: Yes - FNPS admits Spring, Summer and Fall on a rolling basis (2025-2026 FNPS handbook)
spring_2027_deadline: Rolling at FNPS, BUT Clemson Graduate School: international applicants should complete the application by September 15 for Spring (2026-09-15, recommended, passed) and 'I-20s will not be issued after November 15 for Spring Term' (2026-11-15 hard stop; allow about two weeks for the I-20 after admission and documents). Practical target: FNPS admission plus a PI's GRA offer by about 2026-11-01.
spring_deadline_quote: Search-result text of https://www.clemson.edu/admissions/graduate-admissions/apply/international-applicants/: international applicants should finish 'by September 15 for Spring enrollment'; 'I-20s will not be issued after November 15 for Spring Term'. FNPS handbook (quoted by the earlier w2-r3 record): the 'final deadline of acceptance is prior to the last day to register for classes'.
fall_2027_deadline: Rolling at FNPS; the Graduate School's recommended international date for Fall was not captured in this wave
funding_deadline_note: No fixed funding date; GRAs come from individual PIs, so a PI's GRA offer is the real deadline
funding_summary: FNPS handbook (2025-2026, per the earlier wave): GRA is 'the most common mechanism of support', 'awarded on a competitive basis directly by the Principal Investigator of each project'; TAs are less common. This wave found no FNPS faculty grant verified as current and no advertised FNPS GRA opening.
assistantship_types: GRA (main route, paid by individual PIs); GTA less common
international_eligible_for_assistantship: Yes (earlier wave: Clemson international graduate-assistant employment page)
assistantship_deadline: None fixed; depends on the PI
notes: Spring 2027 is still technically possible but very tight because of the 2026-11-15 Spring I-20 cutoff. Also covers the FNPS PhD (https://www.clemson.edu/cafls/academics/graduate/food-nutrition-and-packaging-sciences-phd.html), which has the same rolling rule. Faculty lead from this wave: Hannah Wilson (Assistant Professor, FNPS, based at the Pee Dee REC; Extension community nutrition and stroke-survivor diet quality; see the w3-g professor record). Funded activity seen at Clemson but NOT linked to an FNPS advisor: (1) ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07140952 'Fueling Strong Hearts for a Strong South Carolina' (Clemson lead sponsor, American Heart Association collaborator; online program for stroke survivors in the Pee Dee and Low Country, one arm with a weekly grocery box; SCresearch.org names Ewan Williams as the researcher; a secondary listing says recruiting) (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07140952); (2) Clemson Rural Health diabetes-management program in Orangeburg and nearby counties funded with $600,000 from the Blue Cross Blue Shield of South Carolina Foundation (continuous glucose monitors, produce prescription boxes, medical nutrition therapy), not tied to a named FNPS faculty member (https://news.clemson.edu/clemson-rural-health-launches-diabetes-management-program-in-midlands-south-carolina/). Clemson Extension runs EFNEP (https://www.clemson.edu/extension/efnep/index.html).
